sentences.text: Struthiosaurus was a small armored dinosaur with size estimates ranging from 2 to 3 meters in length and weights between 100 and 400 kilograms.
Its body was protected by sharp bony plates covering the hips, neck, and tail, along with a pair of long spikes on the shoulders and many others along the sides.

Bunzel discovered two rib fragments with a confusing construction; they had two heads, but the upper head was short and positioned so it could not touch the vertebra if the axis was in the usual vertical orientation.
Struthiosaurus is the namesake of the nodosaurid subfamily Struthiosaurinae, whose members are found only in Europe.
The first fossil of Struthiosaurus was discovered in 1859 by geologist Eduard Suess at a coal mine near Wiener Neustadt, Austria, where he found a dinosaur tooth.
The genus Struthiosaurus was formally named in 1871 by Emanuel Bunzel based on a fragment consisting mainly of the posterior end of the skull and braincase.
The discoverer Bunzel sent a drawing and description of the skull fragment to the expert Thomas Huxley in London.
Thomas Huxley agreed that the skull box resembled a bird's, noting it looked more like a bird than anything he had seen before.
Studies published in 2022 suggest that Struthiosaurus had very poor hearing and relied primarily on its armor for defense.
The small flocculus and short lagena in the brain of Struthiosaurus suggest it was a sluggish and solitary animal.
High-resolution CT scans allowed for a digital reconstruction of the Struthiosaurus brain and inner ear shape.

In 1978, Walter Coombs classified Struthiosaurus as a member of the Nodosauridae family. Cladistic analyses suggest that Struthiosaurus is a basal member of the Ankylosauria clade within the Nodosauridae family. Struthiosaurus belongs to the subfamily Struthiosaurinae. Struthiosaurus is classified within the family Nodosauridae. Paleontologists recognize three valid species of Struthiosaurus. Struthiosaurus austriacus was described by Bunzel in 1871 based on the holotype PIWU 2349/6. Nopcsa was the first to understand the fossil represented an armored dinosaur and placed it in Acanthopholididae in 1902. Struthiosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.

Struthiosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Santonian to Maastrichtian stages, in regions including Austria, Romania, France, and possibly Hungary. Struthiosaurus lived in Europe between 83 and 66 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period. Struthiosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
Some studies consider the assignment of Struthiosaurus to Nodosauridae provisional until further study and future discoveries are completed.
